key_insight: Evaluating agentic data-analysis systems requires separating true answer disagreements from grading artifacts, and a three-layer grading cascade can do this reliably.
engineering_relevance: For AI systems that emit code, numbers, and diagnostics, robust evaluation should combine strict extraction, LLM-based lenient judging, and targeted human review to reduce false grading errors.
method: Tested LAMBDA on 153 numerical QRData tasks from DSGym.
Built a three-layer grading cascade: regex matching, lenient LLM grading, and snippet-based human inspection.
Evaluated nudging and answer-template cues to improve run success and grading outcomes.
evidence_signal: Both automated graders achieved 100% observed precision with 0/70 false positives; the lenient grader reached 97% recall, and nudging improved run success from 36% to 97%.
watch_item: Results come from a specific numerical-task benchmark, so the grading pipeline and its gains may not transfer directly to other agentic workflows or task types.
paper_title: Grading the Grader: Lessons from Evaluating an Agentic Data Analysis System
